help.original.heading: Original Keyset Command Summary
help.original.explanation.control_notati: ^ followed by a letter is an abbreviation for pressing and releasing
help.original.explanation.control_modifi: the letter key with the control key also depressed.  You may also press
help.original.explanation.sequential_pre: and release ^ and then press and release the letter key to activate the
help.original.explanation.system_interce: same command in case your system intercepts the control plus key
combination and does not pass it on.  The autoexplore_commands option
help.original.explanation.autoexplore_co: modifies the '<', '>', and 'p' commands.  When that option is off (that
help.original.explanation.autoexplore_de: is the default), the commands act as described below.  When that option
help.original.explanation.autoexplore_cu: is on, '<' or '>' will use the staircase at the player's location if it
help.original.explanation.autoexplore_ne: is the appropriate kind of staircase or will move to the nearest known
help.original.explanation.autoexplore_st: staircase of the appropriate kind if the player is not already at that
help.original.explanation.autoexplore_un: kind of staircase.  'p' will move to the nearest unexplored location
help.original.explanation.autoexplore_en: when the autoexplore_commands option is on.

help.symbols.heading: Symbols On Your Map
help.symbols.overview.categories: Symbols on your map can be broken down into three categories: Features of
help.symbols.overview.features_and_items: the dungeon such as walls, floor, doors, and traps; Objects which can be
help.symbols.overview.items_and_creature: picked up such as treasure, weapons, magical devices, etc; and creatures
help.symbols.overview.creature_mobility: which may or may not move about the dungeon, but are mostly harmful to your
help.symbols.overview.shared_entity_symb: Some symbols are used to represent more than one type of entity, and some
help.symbols.overview.shared_categories_: symbols are used to represent entities in more than one category. The "@"
help.symbols.overview.default_player_sym: symbol (by default) is used to represent the character.
help.symbols.identification.no_memorizat: It will not be necessary to remember all of the symbols and their meanings.
help.symbols.identification.slash_comman: The "slash" command ('/') will identify any character appearing on your
help.symbols.preferences.custom_symbols: Note that you can use a "user pref file" to change any of these symbols to
help.symbols.preferences.familiar_symbol: something you are more comfortable with.
